changes: Rust tokenizer returns ranges and lowercases short schemes into a bounded initialized stack buffer; long schemes use one C++ string allocation followed by Rust in-place lowercasing. This removes the Rust Vec and avoids allocating the C++ scheme to challenge length.

First and later-round decisions each combine scheme comparison and current parameter padding processing into one Rust FFI call. A mismatched scheme does not read parameter bytes. base64_param remains uncached so mutable backing is observed.

Strict decoding writes into an initialized, disjoint private C++ output buffer. Failure discards partial bytes; encoded output is still assigned first and decoded output only on success. Rust performs parsing, validation and decoding.
Safe Rust core uses borrowed slices, including callable direct core policy functions; unsafe is limited to FFI slice construction under documented call-scoped and disjointness contracts.
